backlog.title: Configuration Surface Repair + Type-Safety Gate
backlog.description: Fix two defects identified in end-to-end validation: BUG-001 (the documented settings.json configuration surface is never read — the master enabled off-switch and all 17 knobs are silently ignored because src/index.ts:30 hard-codes setConfig(undefined)) and BUG-002 (the project fails tsc --noEmit due to one stale SessionRuntime test fixture). Core rewind/shrink/checkpoint/audit/cancel functionality, nudges, transforms, filter, and the E22 runaway-loop backstops all work correctly out of the box via defaults; the gap is configurability and type-check cleanliness.

milestones.title: BUG-001: Wire settings.json configuration surface
milestones.description: Make the entire documented configuration surface functional: read the mulligan block from Pi's settings.json (global ~/.pi/agent/settings.json + project-local <cwd>/.pi/settings.json), deep-merge them (project-local wins), and feed the result to setConfig() instead of setConfig(undefined). The downstream consumers (filter.ts, nudges.ts, all five tools) already gate on getConfig().enabled — they need zero changes. The fix is a new src/settings.ts module (Pi-bound, reads files from disk) wired into the index.ts factory and session_start handler.

tasks.title: Create settings-loading module (src/settings.ts)
tasks.description: Create a new Pi-bound module that reads the mulligan config block from Pi's settings.json files. This module is the bridge between Pi's file-based settings system and config.ts's Pi-free validation engine. It reads global settings (via getAgentDir()) and project-local settings (via cwd), deep-merges them (project-local wins), and returns the raw mulligan object for setConfig() to validate. config.ts stays Pi-free by design.

subtasks.title: Implement readSettingsFile() + deepMergeSettings() private helpers
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/system_context.md §1.3 and architecture/pi_api_research.md §C.4. Pi 0.84.1 exports getAgentDir() at runtime (returns ~/.pi/agent/, respects PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR env var). getSettingsPath() is NOT exported at runtime (returns undefined). Settings files are JSON: global at path.join(getAgentDir(), 'settings.json'), project-local at path.join(cwd, '.pi', 'settings.json'). Pi deep-merges settings (settings-manager.js:8-34 deepMergeObjects): both objects → recurse, otherwise project value replaces.
2. INPUT: No inputs — these are leaf utility functions. Uses node:fs readFileSync and node:path join.
3. LOGIC:
   a) readSettingsFile(filePath: string): Record<string, unknown> — Synchronously reads and JSON.parses a settings file. Wrapped in try/catch: missing file, unreadable, or invalid JSON → return {} (empty object, NOT throw). Validates the parsed value is a non-null, non-array object; otherwise returns {}.
   b) deepMergeSettings(global: Record<string, unknown>, project: Record<string, unknown>): Record<string, unknown> — Recursive deep-merge where project-local wins. For each key: if both values are plain objects (typeof 'object', not null, not array), recurse; otherwise project value replaces global value. This must match Pi's deepMergeObjects semantics (see settings-manager.js:8-34). Arrays are REPLACED (not concatenated).
   c) Both helpers are PRIVATE (not exported) — only loadMulliganConfig (S2) calls them.
4. OUTPUT: readSettingsFile returns Record<string, unknown> (never throws). deepMergeSettings returns Record<string, unknown>. Both consumed by P1.M1.T1.S2.
5. MOCKING: For tests, mock node:fs.readFileSync via vitest vi.mock or write real temp files with os.tmpdir(). No Pi mocking needed for these helpers (they are pure fs + merge logic). Test: missing file → {}, invalid JSON → {}, valid JSON → parsed object. deepMerge: overlapping nested objects recurse, non-overlapping keys preserved from both, arrays replace.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on each private helper explaining the merge semantics and fail-open contract. No user-facing doc change — these are internal utilities.

subtasks.title: Implement loadMulliganConfig(cwd?) entry point
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/system_context.md §1.5. The module imports getAgentDir from @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent (confirmed available at runtime). config.ts stays Pi-free (config.ts:160). The module contract: read files → merge → extract .mulligan → return raw object for setConfig() to validate. Fail-open: any error → undefined → validateConfig(undefined) → DEFAULT_CONFIG. The factory (P1.M1.T2.S1) and session_start handler (P1.M1.T2.S2) both call this function.
2. INPUT: cwd?: string — optional project working directory. Falls back to process.cwd() when undefined. At factory time (no ctx), pass undefined or process.cwd(). At session_start (has ctx), pass ctx.cwd.
3. LOGIC:
   a) Import getAgentDir from '@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent'. Import readFileSync from 'node:fs', join from 'node:path'.
   b) Export function loadMulliganConfig(cwd?: string): unknown.
   c) Read global settings: path.join(getAgentDir(), 'settings.json') via readSettingsFile (S1).
   d) Read project-local settings: path.join(cwd ?? process.cwd(), '.pi', 'settings.json') via readSettingsFile (S1).
   e) Deep-merge: deepMergeSettings(global, project) (S1). Project-local wins.
   f) Extract: return (merged as Record<string, unknown>)?.mulligan — may be undefined if the mulligan key is absent (zero-config case → DEFAULT_CONFIG).
   g) ENTIRE body wrapped in try/catch: any error (getAgentDir throws, fs fails, etc.) → return undefined. NEVER throws.
   h) If getAgentDir() import fails or throws, catch and return undefined (fail-open to DEFAULT_CONFIG).
4. OUTPUT: Returns unknown — the raw mulligan object from merged settings, or undefined if absent/error. Consumed by index.ts (P1.M1.T2.S1, P1.M1.T2.S2) which passes it to setConfig().
5. MOCKING: For tests, mock getAgentDir to return a temp directory. Create real settings.json files in temp dirs with os.tmpdir() + fs.mkdirSync. Test cases: (a) no mulligan key → undefined, (b) global-only mulligan → returns global mulligan, (c) project-only → returns project mulligan, (d) both → merged (project wins), (e) missing files → undefined, (f) invalid JSON → undefined, (g) getAgentDir throws → undefined (fail-open).
6. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on loadMulliganConfig explaining: what it reads (global + project-local), merge precedence (project-local wins), fail-open contract (any error → undefined → DEFAULT_CONFIG), and the cwd parameter semantics. This is the module's only export.

tasks.title: Wire settings loading into extension lifecycle (src/index.ts)
tasks.description: Replace the hard-coded setConfig(undefined) at index.ts:30 with real settings loading via loadMulliganConfig(). Wire it at two seams: (1) the factory body (best-effort global + project-local via process.cwd()), and (2) the session_start handler (authoritative project-local via ctx.cwd, re-reads on /reload). After each setConfig() call, re-fire setLogFile(getConfig().log.file) so logging respects the config. Update the stale code comments that admit the gap. Update index.test.ts assertions for the new behavior.

subtasks.title: Wire loadMulliganConfig into factory body + update code comments
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/system_context.md §1.4 (lifecycle asymmetry) and architecture/config_flow_research.md §2. The factory function signature is `export default function (pi: ExtensionAPI): void` — it receives ONLY pi, NO ctx. At factory time, process.cwd() is the best available project directory. The session_start handler (S2) will do the authoritative load with ctx.cwd. The existing factory body (src/index.ts:28-33) calls setConfig(undefined) then setLogFile(getConfig().log.file). The code comment at lines 28-29 explicitly admits the gap: 'v1: validated defaults — no Pi settings accessor in v1; setConfig(undefined) → DEFAULT_CONFIG; reading real settings.mulligan is v1.1'.
2. INPUT: loadMulliganConfig(cwd?: string): unknown from P1.M1.T1.S2. setConfig(raw: unknown) and getConfig() from src/config.ts (unchanged). setLogFile(path) from src/log.ts (unchanged).
3. LOGIC:
   a) Add import: `import { loadMulliganConfig } from './settings.js';` at the top of src/index.ts.
   b) Replace `setConfig(undefined);` (line 30) with `setConfig(loadMulliganConfig());` — no cwd arg means it falls back to process.cwd() inside settings.ts.
   c) Keep `setLogFile(getConfig().log.file);` (line 33) unchanged — it now passes the REAL configured path instead of null.
   d) Update the code comment at lines 28-29 to reflect the new behavior: 'Load + cache config from Pi settings.json (global + project-local via process.cwd()). Fail-open: any error → DEFAULT_CONFIG. Re-read with authoritative ctx.cwd on session_start (see below).'
   e) Update the JSDoc on the factory function (lines 14-27) to remove the 'setConfig(undefined) → DEFAULT_CONFIG' language and reflect that real settings are loaded.
4. OUTPUT: The factory now initializes config from real settings at load time. The existing setLogFile call automatically respects the loaded log.file path. No new exports.
5. MOCKING: In index.test.ts, the factory is tested with a fake ExtensionAPI (makePi()). The test must mock or spy on loadMulliganConfig to verify it is called. Since settings.ts imports getAgentDir from Pi, and the test environment may not have a real settings.json, loadMulliganConfig will return undefined → DEFAULT_CONFIG (fail-open). Test: verify setConfig is called with the return of loadMulliganConfig (not undefined directly). May need vi.mock('./settings.js') to control the return value and assert it was called.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the code comments and JSDoc in src/index.ts as described in step (d)/(e). These are developer-facing docs embedded in source.

subtasks.title: Add config re-read in session_start handler + re-fire setLogFile
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/system_context.md §1.4 and architecture/config_flow_research.md §2. The session_start handler at index.ts currently calls only resetRuntime(ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()). SessionStartEvent has reason: 'startup' | 'reload' | 'new' | 'resume' | 'fork' — all are valid re-read triggers (config may change between sessions, especially on /reload). ExtensionContext has cwd: string (authoritative project dir). After setConfig(), setLogFile(getConfig().log.file) MUST be re-fired because the log destination can change with new settings. The spec (spec/09 §1) promises 're-read on /reload'.
2. INPUT: loadMulliganConfig(cwd?: string) from P1.M1.T1.S2. ctx.cwd from ExtensionContext (the handler's second arg). setConfig, getConfig from config.ts. setLogFile from log.ts. resetRuntime, clearAll from runtime.ts.
3. LOGIC:
   a) In the existing `pi.on('session_start', (_event, ctx) => { ... })` handler body, BEFORE the existing resetRuntime call:
   b) Add: `setConfig(loadMulliganConfig(ctx.cwd));` — authoritative project-local settings.
   c) Add: `setLogFile(getConfig().log.file);` — re-fire log destination after config reload.
   d) Keep the existing: `resetRuntime(ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId());` — unchanged.
   e) Update the code comment above the handler to explain: config is re-read on every session_start (covers startup, /reload, new, resume, fork) using the authoritative ctx.cwd. This fulfills spec/09 §1 're-read on /reload'.
   f) The _event param can remain unused (or rename to _event with a comment that reason is available but all reasons trigger re-read).
4. OUTPUT: The session_start handler now re-reads config with the authoritative cwd and re-points the logger. No new exports.
5. MOCKING: In index.test.ts, the session_start handler test uses a fake ctx (makeCtx()) that exposes only sessionManager.getSessionId(). The test must: (a) extend makeCtx to include cwd (string field), (b) mock loadMulliganConfig to verify it's called with ctx.cwd on session_start, (c) verify setLogFile is re-fired. Test: session_start calls loadMulliganConfig(ctx.cwd), then setConfig result is cached, then setLogFile receives the config's log.file.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the code comment on the session_start handler explaining the config re-read behavior. No user-facing doc change in this subtask.

subtasks.title: Fix stale SessionRuntime fixture in drift_nudge.test.ts
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/tsc_fixture_research.md §3-4. The fixture is at test/drift_nudge.test.ts:238-250 in the rt() helper. It builds a near-complete SessionRuntime literal but omits rewindRefusedTurnIndex (added by P4 drift-nudge-mute work). The cast `as SessionRuntime` on a near-complete object triggers TS2352 under strict:true. The SessionRuntime type (src/runtime.ts) has 10 required fields; the fixture has 9. The missing field rewindRefusedTurnIndex has type number | null and default null (per freshRuntime). All 882 vitest tests pass (vitest transpiles without type-checking); the error only surfaces under tsc --noEmit.
2. INPUT: The existing rt() fixture at test/drift_nudge.test.ts:238-250. The SessionRuntime type from src/runtime.ts (specifically the rewindRefusedTurnIndex: number | null field).
3. LOGIC:
   a) In the rt() helper's returned object literal (between aboveHighWater: above and the closing brace), add the line: `rewindRefusedTurnIndex: null,`.
   b) The value null matches the freshRuntime() default and the field's type (number | null). The shouldHighWater tests that use this fixture never read rewindRefusedTurnIndex, so null is safe.
   c) Do NOT change the cast from `as SessionRuntime` to `as unknown as SessionRuntime` — adding the field is the correct, more honest fix.
4. OUTPUT: The fixture is now type-complete. `npx tsc --noEmit` will exit 0. The 882 existing tests remain unaffected.
5. MOCKING: None needed. The fixture is a plain object literal. Verify: run `npx tsc --noEmit` (must exit 0) and `npx vitest run` (must stay 882/882).
6. DOCS: [Mode A] none — no user-facing/config/API surface change. This is a test-internal fix.

subtasks.title: Update spec/09-configuration.md with implementation note
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/docs_spec_research.md §2.1 and architecture/pi_api_research.md §C.4. spec/09-configuration.md §1 currently says: 'Source: the merged Pi settings object. Mulligan reads settings.mulligan (project-local wins over global via Pi's normal merge).' This implies Pi hands Mulligan an already-merged object. In reality, Pi 0.84.1's ExtensionAPI exposes no settings accessor, so Mulligan reads the files directly from disk (src/settings.ts) and does its own merge. The user-visible behavior is identical.
2. INPUT: The spec/09-configuration.md §1 text. All BUG-001 implementing subtasks.

   a) Read spec/09-configuration.md §1 (Where config is read).
   b) Add an implementation note (sub-bullet or parenthetical) clarifying: 'Implementation: Pi's extension API (v0.84.x) does not expose a settings accessor to extensions. Mulligan therefore reads the settings.json files directly from disk (via getAgentDir() for the global path and the session cwd for project-local), deep-merges them internally (matching Pi's own deepMergeObjects semantics), and extracts settings.mulligan. The user-visible merge behavior is identical to Pi's normal merge.'
   c) Do NOT change the spec's semantic contract — the behavior description is correct. Only add the implementation clarification.
4. OUTPUT: spec/09-configuration.md §1 has an implementation note explaining the direct-file-read approach.
